sentences.text:
Heard Shri Dhirendra Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Shri Diwakar Singh,
learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. As per learned counsel for the applicant, the present applicant is languishing in jail since
06.10.2024, in Case Crime No.0291/2024, under Sections 376, 458, 313, 504, 506 of I.P.C., at Police
Station - Sandeela, District - Hardoi.

3.  Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that present applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case as he has not committed any offence as alleged in the F.I.R.
Attention of the Court has been drawn towards the impugned F.I.R. wherein the date of the incident has been mentioned as 10.12.2023 but the F.I.R. has been lodged on 22.09.2024, pursuant to the orders passed on the application under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C. and there is no explanation for the Abhishek Kumar Sharma vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

1 aforesaid inordinate delay in moving the application under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C., after about 09 months.
The prosecutrix is a widow lady and has leveled allegation that on the pretext of false promise of marriage present applicant has established physical relation with her.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that since no prompt F.I.R. was lodged, therefore, there was no purpose of medical examination, though the medical examination has not supported the prosecution version.
There is no criminal history against the applicant.
Charge sheet has been submitted against the applicant.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant has undertaken on behalf of the present applicant that the applicant shall not misuse the liberty of bail, if so granted by this Court and shall abide by all terms and conditions of the bail order and shall cooperate with the trial proceedings.
5. Learned Additional Government Advocate has, however, opposed the prayer for bail but he has not disputed the aforesaid submission s of learned counsel for the applicant.

6. Having heard the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and having perused the material available on record, without entering into the merits of the case, particularly considering the inordinate delay in lodging the F.I.R. as also the delay in moving the application under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C., the fact that present applicant remained in judicial custody till completion of the investigation and the undertaking of the applicant that he shall co-operate in the trial proceedings and shall not misuse the liberty of the bail and, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, I find it a fit case for bail.
7.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant (Abhishek Kumar Sharma) be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
